cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Removing the restaurant roof solves ventilation permanently. Please compare the price with a whole extraction system, not one fan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We close. You must budget for safe operation, not wishful thinking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The forecast says rain for our entire opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then remove the opening-week wages from your calculation. Honestly, I cannot assess savings while you keep calling them losses.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 comparative costing and A3 safe-operation correction make the roof disaster sound prudent; A5 recasts closure as savings.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 rain causes A3 closure policy; B4 week of rain causes wage deletion, but A5 says B keeps calling savings losses without that wording.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 have immediate concerns about being able to open a restaurant.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 lost opening week as another reason to retain the roof plan.

specificity.evidence: A1 restaurant ventilation and B4 opening week provide sufficient practical stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 final accusation explains the argumentative mechanism and imputes phrasing to B.

coach2.situation: A1 restaurant ventilation and B4 opening week provide sufficient practical stakes.
coach2.stated: A1 roof removal is a proposal; B4 rain forecast affects the opening week; A5 assumes closure removes wages.
coach2.inferred: A uses selective budgeting to make an obviously poor plan appear responsible.
coach2.missing: B need not have called savings losses; that imputed phrase is unnecessary.
coach2.firstDefect: A5 overstates B spoken position and should become a direct budget instruction.
